extracted.intended_audience: young tradesmen and general readers seeking practical moral, financial, health, and self-improvement advice
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of prescriptive maxims and short essays giving actionable rules for running a business, preserving health and sleep, cultivating virtue, and valuing mathematics; aimed at guiding personal conduct and professional habits. Contains concrete, sometimes enumerated rules and examples (e.g., 'Advice to a Young Tradesman', 'Rules of Health', 'The Art of Procuring Pleasant Dreams').

rubrics_metrics.name: Time is money
rubrics_metrics.description: He that can earn ten shillings a day by his labour, and goes abroad or sits idle one half of that day... has really spent, or, rather, thrown away, five shillings besides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat lost working hours as lost earnings; when evaluating leisure vs work, account for the foregone wages as a real cost. Example: an hour away from profitable work costs the income you would have earned in that hour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit is money
rubrics_metrics.description: If a man lets his money lie in my hands after it is due, he gives me the interest, or so much as I can make of it during that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the economic value of having use of others' money; good credit management is equivalent to capital. Maintain and use credit advantageously but beware of letting others have your funds overdue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money is prolific (compound returns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Money can beget money, and its offspring can beget more, and so on... Five shillings turned is six, turned again it is seven and threepence, and so on till it becomes a hundred pounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinvest profits; small capital properly turned can compound significantly over time. This supports saving and reinvestment as a strategic rule for growing wealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small sums multiply into large capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Six pounds a year is but a groat a day... a man of credit may, on his own security, have the constant possession and use of a hundred pounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand how small daily savings or small regular returns can be leveraged into larger working capital via credit or reinvestment. Treat modest regular returns as meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a punctual paymaster
rubrics_metrics.description: The good paymaster is lord of another man's purse. He that is known to pay punctually and exactly to the time he promises, may at any time raise all the money his friends can spare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize paying debts exactly and on time to preserve and extend access to credit. Reputation for punctual payment is a practical asset; avoid holding borrowed money beyond promised time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect your public image and avoid idle diversions
rubrics_metrics.description: The sound of your hammer at five in the morning or nine at night... but if he sees you at a billiard-table, or hears your voice at a tavern when you should be at work, he sends for his money the next day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard against behaviors that signal negligence to creditors or customers. Small public signs (appearance, hours, visible leisure) influence others' willingness to trust your credit and business reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep exact accounts to curb hidden expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep an exact account for some time both of your expenses and your income... you will discover how wonderfully small, trifling expenses mount up to large sums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track particulars of income and expenses to reveal waste and opportunities to save. Use bookkeeping early to change spending habits before they compound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry and frugality: the road to wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: The way to wealth... depends chiefly on two words, industry and frugality; that is, waste neither time nor money, but make the best use of both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine consistent work (industry) with disciplined saving (frugality). Ethical acquisition ('all he can honestly') plus saving what remains is presented as a practical rule to become rich.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eat and drink in quantities suited to your constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Eat and drink such an exact quantity as the constitution of thy body allows of, in reference to the services of the mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust food and drink to physical constitution and occupational demands (those who study should eat less than manual labourers). Find and maintain a steady quantity and quality appropriate to your body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep quantity and quality of food constant
rubrics_metrics.description: The exact quantity and quality being found out, is to be kept to constantly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once you determine what your constitution requires, avoid frequent changes; stability helps digestion and health. Avoid excesses and irregularities that disrupt bodily balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excess in all things
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess in all other things whatever, as well as in meat and drink, is also to be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderation is a general rule: temper appetite and behaviour to promote long life, health, and mental vigour. Apply to food, drink, and other habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust diet for age, sickness, and temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: Youth, age, and the sick require a different quantity. And so do those of contrary complexions; for that which is too much for a phlegmatic man is not sufficient for a choleric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalize dietary rules: one size does not fit all. Consider age, current health, and temperament when setting intake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eat for necessity, not pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: Eat for necessity, not pleasure; for lust knows not where necessity ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control appetite by rational limits: eating should meet the stomach's needs rather than be driven by indulgence, to promote health and longevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve health by due exercise and temperance (for pleasant dreams)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary to be careful in preserving health, by due exercise and great temperance; for in sickness the imagination is disturbed, and disagreeable... ideas are apt to present themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular exercise and moderation in food are primary preventive measures for avoiding nightmares and disturbed sleep. Exercise should precede meals rather than follow them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise before meals, not immediately after
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise should precede meals, not immediately follow them; the first promotes, the latter, unless moderate, obstructs digestion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer pre-meal physical activity to aid digestion and healthy sleep; avoid heavy physical inactivity immediately following substantial food intake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hearty suppers after full dinners
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppers are not bad if we have not dined; but restless nights naturally follow hearty suppers after full dinners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have eaten a large midday meal, avoid another large evening meal; timing and size of meals affect sleep quality and risk of grave consequences in extreme cases (cited anecdotes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure fresh air in the bedchamber
rubrics_metrics.description: Another means of preserving health... is the having a constant supply of fresh air in your bedchamber. It has been a great mistake, the sleeping in rooms exactly closed, and in beds surrounded by curtains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sleeping in closed, poorly ventilated rooms; allow airflow to remove 'perspirable matter' and prevent discomfort or disease. Example: open a window or avoid heavy curtains when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use thinner, more porous bedclothes
rubrics_metrics.description: By using thinner and more porous bedclothes, which will suffer the perspirable matter more easily to pass through them, we are less incommoded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose bedding materials and coverings that allow evaporation and air exchange to reduce accumulation of exhaled moisture and associated sleep disturbance.

rubrics_metrics.name: If awakened by bed-heat, air and cool the bed before returning
rubrics_metrics.description: When you are awakened by this uneasiness... get out of bed, beat up and turn your pillow, shake the bedclothes well, with at least twenty shakes, then throw the bed open and leave it to cool;... walk about your chamber till your skin has had time to discharge its load.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical method for restoring comfortable sleep after waking hot: ventilate bedding, shake and cool bed, walk undressed until perspiration subsides, then return. Alternative (less effective): lift bedclothes with arm/leg to draw in air.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shifting beds or having two beds helps restore sleep
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who do not love trouble, and can afford to have two beds, will find great luxury in rising, when they wake in a hot bed, and going into the cool one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If feasible, use a second cool bed or bedding to recover from overheated sleep. This is recommended for luxury and sometimes for fevers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position pillow and limbs to avoid pressure and discomfort
rubrics_metrics.description: Care must be taken, when you lie down, to dispose your pillow so as to suit your manner of placing your head, and to be perfectly easy; then place your limbs so as not to bear inconveniently hard upon one another...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange sleeping posture and pillow to avoid ongoing pressure points that may cause discomfort during sleep and provoke unpleasant dreams. Small adjustments can prevent later disturbance.

rubrics_metrics.name: A good conscience aids pleasant dreams
rubrics_metrics.description: But, though they will generally prove effectual in producing the end intended, there is a case in which the most punctual observance of them will be totally fruitless... The case is, when the person who desires to have pleasant dreams has not taken care to preserve, what is necessary above all things, A GOOD CONSCIENCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral and psychological state influences quality of dreams; practical sleep-hygiene rules may fail if the mind is troubled by guilt or conscience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-denial is not the essence of virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: It is commonly asserted, that without self-denial there is no virtue... If self-denial be the essence of virtue, then it follows that the man who is naturally temperate, just, &c., is not virtuous...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish virtue from mere self-denial: performing virtuous acts from natural inclination still counts as virtue. Self-denial has value when it resists temptations toward vice, but natural goodness is not less virtuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish virtue from merit (desert)
rubrics_metrics.description: But perhaps it may be said, that by the word 'virtue' in the above assertion is meant merit... By merit is understood desert; and when we say a man merits, we mean that he deserves praise or reward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand ethical evaluations: merit attaches to actions against inclination (praiseworthy overcoming), whereas virtue describes the character whether acting from inclination or resistance. Use this distinction when judging moral worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics is essential practical knowledge (arithmetic for commerce)
rubrics_metrics.description: No business, commerce, trade, or employment whatsoever... can be managed and carried on without the assistance of numbers; for by these the trader computes the value of all sorts of goods...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize arithmetic competency for anyone engaged in trade or commerce; evaluate business competence partially by facility with numbers and bookkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometry underpins arts, mechanics, navigation, and surveying
rubrics_metrics.description: That which is concerned about measure in general... is called geometry... it is by the assistance of this science that geographers... the ingenious mariner is instructed how to guide a ship... architects take their just measures for the structure of buildings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat geometry as foundational for practical crafts: architecture, engineering, navigation, surveying, and mapmaking depend on geometric principles. Encourage study of geometry for practical technical competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical demonstrations train the mind for exact reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical demonstrations are a logic of as much or more use than that commonly learned at schools, serving to a just formation of the mind, enlarging its capacity, and strengthening it so as to render the same capable of exact reasoning...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value mathematics not only for direct applications but for cultivating precise, disciplined thinking transferable to non-mathematical problems. When evaluating education, include mathematical training as cognitive development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid wasting life; be usefully occupied
rubrics_metrics.description: What have I done all this time for God or man?... He applied himself to gain some useful knowledge... He lived many following years with the character of a worthy man... Are there not numbers... whose lives thus run to utter waste, without the least tendency to usefulness?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge a life by usefulness and contribution; avoid habitual indolence and disengagement. Practical remedy: self-reflection, acquisition of knowledge, service to neighbours and country. Example given: a man who reformed after reflection became exemplary.
